messages.subject: ldply, merge and lists
parts:
Dear All,

I am preparing my data for a scatterplot of biological patient tests of baseline value vs values taken at different visits.

I have a list of 30+ dataframes and here is toy example:

bio <- structure(list(a = structure(list(subjid = structure(c(1L, 1L,
1L, 1L), .Label = c("N1", "N2", "N3"), class = "factor"), visit = structure(1:4, .Label = c("V0",
"V1", "V2", "V3"), class = "factor"), result = c(5L, 8L, 9L,
10L)), .Names = c("subjid", "visit", "result"), row.names = c(NA,
4L), class = "data.frame"), b = structure(list(subjid = structure(c(2L,
2L, 2L), .Label = c("N1", "N2", "N3"), class = "factor"), visit = structure(c(1L,
2L, 4L), .Label = c("V0", "V1", "V2", "V3"), class = "factor"),
    result = c(40L, 50L, 52L)), .Names = c("subjid", "visit",
"result"), row.names = 5:7, class = "data.frame"), c = structure(list(
    subjid = structure(c(3L, 3L, 3L), .Label = c("N1", "N2",
    "N3"), class = "factor"), visit = structure(1:3, .Label = c("V0",
    "V1", "V2", "V3"), class = "factor"), result = c(100L, 110L,
    111L)), .Names = c("subjid", "visit", "result"), row.names = 8:10, class = "data.frame")), .Names = c("a",
"b", "c"))
library(Hmisc)
library(plyr)
biovo <- lapply(bio,subset, visit == "V0",select=c(subjid,visit,result))
biovo <- lapply(biovo,upData, rename= c(result = "baseline"))
bioall <- lapply(bio,subset, visit != "V0")
#
test <- ldply(bioall, merge, biovo , by ="subjid", all.x=TRUE)

so the last line tries to merge the list (bioall) of all tests with all (non baseline) visit with the list of baseline values.

I get this error message
> test <- ldply(bioall, merge, biovo , by = "subjid", all.x=TRUE)
Erreur dans fix.by(by.y, y) : 'by' must specify valid column(s)

I suspect this is because I have a list and I should be using a list index but I don't see how to do that.

By the way I get a different error message when I use my real data:

> test <- ldply(bioall,merge,biovo,by="subjid",all.x=TRUE)
Erreur dans data.frame(ast = list(subjid = c("0101MT", "0102MJ", "0103BC",  :
  arguments imply differing number of rows: 516, 519, 515

Thanks for any help with this. maybe I need to do that a completely different way ?

Best wishes, JL

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: ldply, merge and lists
parts:
Firstly, thank you for the reproducible example. You don't really need
Hmisc here; the rename() function in the reshape package also works.
Assuming that James' solution is what you wanted, here's a pure
plyr/reshape way to do it, as Hadley gets sad when we mix **ply with
apply family functions, and we certainly don't want that :)

library('reshape')
library('plyr')
biovo <- llply(bio, function(d) subset(d, visit == 'V0'))
biovo <- llply(biovo, rename, c(result = 'baseline', visit = 'visit0'))
bioall <- llply(bio, subset, visit != "V0")
# join() assumes left joins by default
# => no need for an all.x = argument
out <- llply(names(bioall), function(x) join(bioall[[x]], biovo[[x]],
by = 'subjid'))
# a little post-merge cleanup:
llply(out, function(d) mutate(d, diff = result - baseline, visit0 = NULL))

After seeing all of these llply() machinations, it seems more
efficient to code all of this up into a function that can be processed
in one call:

f <- function(d) {
# require('reshape')
# require('plyr')
d1 <- subset(d, visit == 'V0')
d2 <- subset(d, visit != 'V0')
d1 <- rename(d1, c(result = 'baseline', visit = 'visit0'))
dm <- join(d2, d1, by = 'subjid')
dm <- mutate(dm, diff = result - baseline, visit0 = NULL)
dm
}

llply(bio, f)

HTH,
Dennis

messages.subject: Re: ldply, merge and lists
parts: > Or even easier, just add identifier columns and use a single join.

I ended up with this, but it requires renaming most of the columns and
NULLing a few of them out post-merge.

g2 <- function(d) {
# Define an indicator for baseline and subsequent visits
d <- mutate(d, vis0 = visit == 'V0')
v <- join(subset(d, vis0), subset(d, !vis0), by = 'subjid')
names(v) <- c('subjid', 'visit0', 'baseline', 'vis0',
'visit', 'result', 'vis1')
v <- mutate(v, visit0 = NULL, vis0 = NULL, vis1 = NULL,
diff = result - baseline)
v
}
llply(bio, g2)

I didn't see a way to use the equivalent of split() to form the two
arguments for join() - I tried several things without success. In the
end, the kludge above at least gave me two data frames I could use as
input. Assuming there's a better way, I'd like to see it.

Dennis

messages.subject: Re: ldply, merge and lists
parts:
> I didn't see a way to use the equivalent of split() to form the two
> arguments for join() - I tried several things without success. In the
> end, the kludge above at least gave me two data frames I could use as
> input. Assuming there's a better way, I'd like to see it.

I meant collapse the data first, and then do a single join. Like this:

library(reshape2)
library(plyr)

biom <- melt(bio, id = 1:3)

first <- mutate(subset(biom, visit == "V0"), visit = NULL)
names(first)[2] <- "first_result"

subseq <- subset(biom, visit != "V0")

join(subseq, first, by = c("subjid", "L1"))

Hadley
